summary.text: Nicholas Begich is the Republican incumbent seeking a second term in Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat, first elected in 2024. A Chugiak resident born in Anchorage, he worked at Ford Motor Company before returning to Alaska in 2004 and starting technology and investment businesses, including FarShore Partners and Dashfire. He previously ran for Anchorage City Council (2016) and for this House seat in 2022.

paragraphs.text: Born in Anchorage, Alaska, and raised by his maternal grandparents, according to his congressional website; he lives in Chugiak with his wife, Dharna, and their son.
Earned a B.B.A. in entrepreneurship from Baylor University (1999) and an M.B.A. from Indiana University-Bloomington (2002).
According to his congressional website, was recruited by Ford Motor Company, where he worked in technology, finance and product development, before he and his wife returned to Alaska in 2004.
Founded FarShore Partners, a technology development company, and co-founded Dashfire, a startup investment firm; his congressional website also says he has served as a startup coach and mentor.

Completed a fellowship with the Club for Growth and co-chaired the Alaska Republican Party's Finance Committee and Rep. Don Young's 2020 re-election campaign. His congressional website also lists prior work with the Alaska Policy Forum and service as a board director of Matanuska Telecom Association.
Ran for Anchorage City Council (District 2, Seat A) in 2016 and lost to incumbent Amy Demboski, 57.7% to 41.7%.
Ran for Alaska's at-large U.S. House seat in 2022, finishing third in the first round of the ranked-choice count behind Mary Peltola and Sarah Palin; Peltola won.
Won the 2024 general election for the at-large U.S. House seat over Mary Peltola, 51.2% to 48.8% after ranked-choice tabulation, and took office in 2025.
Committee assignments for 2025-2026 include Natural Resources (Vice Chair of the Energy and Mineral Resources subcommittee), Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology.
